history.note: Baseline: every client released so far speaks this protocol; minimum stays 1.0.0.

Reviews accept an optional statement verdict, and facts gain other proofs with their own routes and a proof_disputed status. Older clients send no statement verdict, which keeps the previous meaning of their reviews, and they do not read fact statuses.

Adds the notation task kind, given only to clients that list it in features, its routes, and a definition status that clients do not read. Extraction context gains a notation key that older clients ignore.
Proof searches and questions also receive the agreed notation, and a fact's statement in it. These are extra context keys that older clients ignore.
Facts gain a stars count, the list a starred flag and a fact its starred_by list, and stars have their own routes for people. Clients ignore these fields.
Notation entries take comments, given to notation tasks in context.notation[].comments, an extra key older clients ignore.

A compact list in columns and a match route for the interface, an ETag on the list, local notation entries and instance variants. The default list is unchanged, and the new notation fields are extra keys older clients ignore.
Rewrites accept a local_notation, entries a facts list, the notation list adds shared symbols, and notation reviews receive local_notation. All are optional or extra keys that older clients ignore.
Auth recognises audit keys (oqa_), which sign nobody in. Personal keys and sessions behave as before, so AI clients are unaffected.
Consolidation is a new task kind offered only to clients that send the consolidate feature; facts gain an additive topics field; extract, notation and other tasks are unchanged for older clients.

Procedures are offered with a recipe only to clients that send the procedures feature; older clients still get ask, notation and consolidate without a recipe and post to the same endpoints as before, which are unchanged.
Questions to the AI now receive fact statements and the cited facts in full: new fields in the context, which clients copy into task.json as they are

Cited results and proved facts: new fields in fact data and task contexts, a new cite proposal in the consolidation schema sent as a recipe, and a new source_check procedure that clients from 1.12.0 run only once their user turns it on. Older clients keep their own consolidation schema and their reviews are still accepted
A fact returned by GET /api/facts/{id} adds the agreed notation of the project: a new field that clients ignore

Consolidation confidence and undo: clients from 1.12.0 receive the new schema with the recipe and give a confidence; older clients send none, so their proposals wait for people as before. The answer to a consolidation post adds an applied list that older clients ignore
A new read endpoint for proof searches (proving-context); clients before 1.14.0 do not call it, and 1.14.0 continues without it on an older platform
New endpoints for the native prover, used only by clients from 1.15.0; the proving context adds a usable field that older clients ignore
A progress proposal in the consolidation schema sent with the recipe, and a continuous lead option that only clients from 1.16.0 request; older clients keep working as before

Notation joins the consolidation as a new proposal kind, carried in the recipe's instructions and schema, so clients from 1.12.0 run it unchanged; older clients post consolidation proposals without it, which the server still accepts. Notation entries gain who decided them.

Source checks of cited results are now queued automatically; they are the existing source_check procedure, run by clients from 1.13.0 by default and never given to older clients. The facts batch answer gains source_checks_queued, which clients ignore.

Cited results nobody accepted are now usable by the native prover unless disputed or contradicted by their source check; clients read the usable flag from the server, so 1.17.0 follows the new rule with its older wording. Reading suggestions gain citations to check. Client 1.18.0 updates the prover's instructions.

Automatic source checks become batches: a source_check task without source_type carries the source_check_batch recipe, which clients from 1.13.0 run generically like any recipe; requests for one fact keep the single recipe. Task lists gain a subject for batches, and activity lines gain count and more.

Claims now follow a priority and wait for the tasks a task depends on; clients still claim and answer the same way and only see a different order. The AI overview gains groups, and tasks gain priority, group and waits_for, which clients ignore.

The consolidation reads how many facts use each one, notation symbols written with dollars match their project entries, and the audit notation says who decided each entry. Clients read these through recipes or ignore them; client 1.19.0 adds extraction labels and generation times, which the server already accepted.

Upkeep becomes sweeps: source checks and rewrites in the project notation are one task per kind, offered only to clients that run recipes (from 1.12.0), which run the new notation_rephrase_batch variant generically. Older clients no longer receive automatic per-fact rewrites; a person's request for one fact still reaches them. The facts batch answer loses source_checks_queued, which clients did not read.

The consolidation and notation recipes say that different wordings of one notion are one meaning; the notation list gains a clash count per entry. Clients run recipes as sent and ignore the new field.

Two new procedures (rewrite_check, second_reading) and their sweeps, new optional fields (bib suggestions added/auto_added/verified_by, rephrasing check_ai_*, suggestion second_*), and earlier_rewrite_problem in rewrite batches. Older clients ignore unknown procedures unless their user turns them on, and every existing route keeps its shape; client 1.20.0 turns the two procedures on by default.
